html:
The Knight in the Panther's Skin is the national epic of Georgia, a long poem written around 1200 by Shota Rustaveli, who dedicated it to Queen Tamar.

It tells of two knights, Avtandil and Tariel, set in Arabia and India, who help each other and rescue Tariel's beloved Nestan-Darejan. Its themes are friendship, loyalty and love, and it praises a woman ruler. It is written in quatrains of sixteen syllable lines. For centuries Georgian brides received a copy as part of their dowry, and many Georgians still know parts by heart. The first printed edition appeared in Tbilisi in 1712. It is written in the Georgian script and is the best known work of Georgian literature.
sum: The Knight in the Panther's Skin is the national epic of Georgia, a long poem written around 1200 by Shota Rustaveli, who dedicated it to Queen Tamar.
